nodes.question: B02_Q03
nodes.need: the radius for each floor: base share + top share
nodes.hint: Maths › Operators. Watch for: Multiply first, then add: the two shares add up to one value per floor.
nodes.correct: Addition adds the base share and the top share, giving a radius that tapers smoothly from base to top.
nodes.stage: Taper the size: A radius and a fillet for every floor, blending from the base values to the top values. Blend = base × (1 - t) + top × t. At the base t = 0, so you get the base radius; at the top t = 1, the top radius.

wrong.multiplication: Multiplying the shares would shrink the middle floors to almost nothing.
wrong.*: This step needs the sum of the two shares.

nodes.question: B02_Q08
nodes.need: the surface area of the tower
nodes.hint: Surface › Analysis. Area works on curves, surfaces and solids. Watch for: Set Total twist to 0: the area drops, because twisting stretches the skin.
nodes.correct: Area measures the tower's envelope in square feet and finds its centroid. The Panel shows the number.
nodes.stage: Check your result: A number that proves the mass is right. Read outputs as data, not just as a picture. Area gives the surface area (sf) and the centroid.

wrong.volume: Volume would be a good check too, but this step reads the envelope area.
wrong.*: This step needs the surface area of the solid.

nodes.question: B02_Q07
nodes.need: a closed solid: lids on the loft's open top and bottom
nodes.hint: Surface › Util. The loft is a tube with two flat openings. Watch for: Only flat (planar) openings can be capped.
nodes.correct: Cap Holes fills the planar openings at the top and bottom, turning the lofted tube into a closed solid.
nodes.stage: Close the mass: A closed solid (Brep): the tower mass. Loft leaves the top and bottom open; Cap Holes adds flat lids to planar openings.

wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces would make loose discs, not one joined solid.
wrong.brepJoin: Brep Join joins existing pieces: there are no lids yet to join.
wrong.*: This step needs to close the loft's openings.

nodes.question: B02_Q06
nodes.need: one surface through all the floor outlines
nodes.hint: Surface › Freeform. It takes a list of section curves. Watch for: The outlines must arrive in floor order, base to roof: Range already guarantees that.
nodes.correct: Loft skins one surface through every floor outline in order.
nodes.stage: Skin the floors: One surface through every floor outline. With many section curves, Loft makes one smooth skin that follows every floor's size and twist.

wrong.extrude: Extrude pushes one curve along a vector: it can't connect different profiles.
wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces only fills flat outlines: you'd get separate floor discs.
wrong.sweep1: Sweep1 needs a rail curve to follow. Here there are only section curves.
wrong.*: This step needs a surface through section curves.

nodes.question: B02_Q02
nodes.need: the total tower height: Floors × Floor-to-floor
nodes.hint: Maths › Operators. Watch for: This replaces B01's Unit Z + Move: every floor gets its own height in one go.
nodes.correct: Multiplication gives the total height; a second Multiplication scales it by t to get every floor's height.
nodes.stage: Floor levels: A centre point at the height of every floor. Total height = Floors × Floor-to-floor. Each floor's height = t × total. Construct Point turns those heights into points.

wrong.addition: Addition gives Floors + Floor-to-floor, not the stacked height.
wrong.*: This step needs the product of two numbers.

nodes.question: B02_Q04
nodes.need: one outline per floor from centre points, radii and fillets
nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. The same node as Level A. Watch for: One point, one radius and one fillet per floor: the lists line up item by item.
nodes.correct: Polygon draws one outline per floor, each at its own centre point with its own radius and fillet.
nodes.stage: Floor outlines: One outline per floor, at its own height and size. Polygon accepts lists: a list of centre points and a list of radii draws one outline per item.

nodes.question: B02_Q01
nodes.need: one value per floor, evenly spaced from 0 to 1
nodes.hint: Sets › Sequence. It divides a domain into a number of equal steps. Watch for: The second Range has its domain set to 1 to 0. That makes the mirror list (1 - t) with no extra maths.
nodes.correct: Range divides the 0–1 domain into Floors equal steps, so every floor gets its own t value.
nodes.stage: One value per floor: A list from 0 (base) to 1 (top), one value per floor, and its mirror from 1 down to 0. Range splits a domain into equal steps. Every node after it now works on the whole list: all floors at once.

wrong.series: Series counts up by a fixed step size: you'd have to work out the step yourself. Range takes the domain and the number of steps.
wrong.random: Random gives scattered values: floors must be evenly spaced.
wrong.*: This step needs evenly spaced values between 0 and 1.

nodes.question: B02_Q05
nodes.need: each floor outline turned by its own angle
nodes.hint: Transform › Euclidean. Geometry, Angle and Plane. Watch for: Degrees is switched on for the A input; without it 90 would mean 90 radians.
nodes.correct: Rotate turns every floor outline by its own angle around its own centre point: a smooth twist up the tower.
nodes.stage: Twist each floor: Each outline turned a little more than the one below. Angle per floor = t × Total twist: the base turns 0° and the roof the full twist. Rotate pairs each outline with its own angle and centre.

wrong.move: Move shifts geometry. The outline has to turn, not shift.
wrong.mirror: Mirror flips across a plane: a jump, not a gradual twist.
wrong.orient: Orient maps geometry from one plane to another: much more set-up than a simple turn.
wrong.*: This step needs a transform that turns geometry by an angle.

check.prompt: The twist angle goes into which input of Rotate?
check.hint: G = geometry, A = angle, P = plane (the centre) to rotate around.
check.correct: A is the angle, read in degrees because Degrees is switched on.

wrong.G: G is the geometry: the outline is already connected.
wrong.P: P is the rotation plane: the centre point goes there.

check.prompt: The centre point goes into which input of Rotate?
check.hint: A rotation needs a centre to turn around.
check.correct: P is the plane to rotate around: a point there means 'turn around this point'.

wrong.A: A is the angle: that's the twist value.
wrong.*: That input isn't the centre of rotation.
